current.title: Invasive Species Now Cost The World $423 Billion A Year
current.hook: That's more than most countries make.
current.closing: Nature sent the world a bill nobody budgeted for.
current.question: Ever seen an invasive species mess up your own backyard? Tell me below.

segments.say: The global bill for invasive species has roughly quadrupled every decade since 1970 -- reaching 423 billion dollars a year.
Almost all of it, over 90 percent, pays for damage already done. Barely 10 percent goes to stopping the next invasion.

segments.topic: how many invasive species there really are
segments.say: Over 37 thousand alien species have taken hold worldwide. Only about 3.5 thousand of them are the ones actually causing the damage.

held_for: judge: Three charts and a stock seesaw with Data perched on each; the quadrupling bill is never shown as anything physical, and the finale replays seg3's numbers as a meaningless race of duplicate mascots.

judge.one_line: Three charts and a stock seesaw with Data perched on each; the quadrupling bill is never shown as anything physical, and the finale replays seg3's numbers as a meaningless race of duplicate mascots.
problems: Hook (hook@0.3 to 2.2) is a static bar chart building slowly behind the title; nothing grabs attention in frame 1.
seg1 shows a thin line in a large empty frame with a false 'and back again' label, and Data cheers at a cost peak.
seg2 settles at 88.7% while the narration says 'over 90 percent', and 76.4% plus 8.5% mid-animation reads as broken.
Data perches on bars, on the line end, on the seesaw and on the bubble in every scene; he never performs a bit.
seg4 duplicates the mascot into two racing lanes, repeating seg3's data with no meaning, and its grey lane label is too small to read.
Only the seesaw is more than a chart; nothing is made of invasive species or of a bill.
fixes: Open on motion that carries the claim: a $423B invoice slamming down, or a pile of bills bursting upward, before any chart appears.
Rebuild seg1 as a compounding bill that grows fourfold each decade and fills the frame height; delete the 'and back again' caption.
Settle the seg2 seesaw on values that match the narration (over 90% vs about 10%), and have Data pile weight onto the damage side or be flung off the prevention end.
In seg3, draw the 37K as a swarm of species icons with the 3.5K harmful ones lighting up, instead of two bubbles.
Replace the seg4 duplicate-mascot race with a real payoff tied to the closing line (the bill arriving), and make the lane labels large and high-contrast.

rules: TITLE or HOOK must contain a consequential NUMBER from the data below (the gate refuses a title+hook with no digit in either).

TITLE must be a PREMISE, not a searchable noun phrase: more than five words, or a number, or a question mark, or a tension word. 'Oldest Written Languages' is the failure; 'Why 3 of the 5 Oldest Scripts Are Still Unreadable' is the shape.

Every segment's TOPIC (a 2-4 word on-screen label) must share at least one real word with the TITLE — the gate checks a keyword bridge from each segment to the headline. Rename the topic, or write the title so it names what the segments are about.

Every NUMBER you say in a segment's SAY must be one that segment's data can show: a listed value, a difference between two of them, a percent change, a share of the total, or the same value in a bigger unit. A number from nowhere is refused — a guard derives every spoken quantity from the listed points.
Keep every number that is already correct. Do not add a country, company or person the data does not name.
Each SAY is one spoken sentence or two, at most 40 words, and says its beat's headline number out loud.
TOPIC labels are printed on the video: at most 4 words, no clause.
